text: Understanding Git branching is important for modern software development. A branch lets you work on new features without changing the main code. Developers often create feature branches to build and test their work safely. When the feature is ready, they merge it back into the main branch. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request so others can review the changes. This keeps the version control workflow organized and reduces mistakes. Using branches, merging, and pull requests together helps teams collaborate smoothly and keep their project stable. Learning this process is a key skill for anyone working with Git.
